_about: Italian East Africa and the Sahara posts, June 1940 to December 1941: the garrisons the far chart did not have (the design director's ruling C of 11:40Z and his acceptance of 13:09Z, 22 November 2026, on the historian's iea-sahara-1940-41.md, sources E1 to E30). Until these rows East Africa stood empty on the far chart, Britain's Sudan, Kenya and Somaliland too, and the fronts there read hundreds to one. Laid as data, as found, behind the far switch (far-rows.ts lays this file last); nothing is fitted to a result. Written by /mnt/project-files/pacific-six/far-africa-make.py and kept by hand after.
_form: A row is the chart's dated row: month, nation, formation, kind, divisions, place, words. 'est' is the row's size by date as a share of its divisions (worth = divisions x est), the record's men at 15,000 to 1.0. 'until' with 'holds' is the row's last month: at the book's stops the row ends in that month by date; where the book is not kept it stands while its place is held and ends when it is lost (game.ts, lentOver). 'ends': 'surrender' gives the card a surrender's words where a lent row's would say it left for other fronts. 'mark' is the historian's mark where it is not F: L likely, D derived, U uncertain; 'memory' is a row from memory, which no card prints until it is checked.
_italy: Italy's army on 1 June 1940 by its six commands and the headquarters, 17.1 (255,950 men, [E6]): headquarters 0.5, Eritrea 2.8, Amhara 4.0, Shoa 3.6, Galla-Sidamo 2.1, Harar 2.5, Somalia 1.6. The pages give the commands and their seats, not their borders: each command's worth is shared evenly over the far-side places the file lists as its ground, so that each place has its holder and its own last month (D, the builder's arithmetic). All forces from 1 August 1940, 24.7 (371,053 men): each row grows in the same share from month 12 (D). From month 21 the file's 'over 80,000 in the field': Gondar 2.7 and Galla-Sidamo 2.5, the latter shared evenly by Jimma and Lekemti (D); Assab from 21 at the 582 men taken there, 0.04 (D). From 23 Gondar alone, 2.7. Three forces are rows of their own, each taken out of its command's worth so that the sums stand ('_gains'): the Kassala force, 0.4 of Eritrea's (the command's five places share the other 2.4, and from month 12 the command's growth), the Gallabat force, 0.05 of Amhara's and of Gondar's 2.7 from 21, and Nasi's force, 1.95 of Harar's from month 12. A force keeps its record figure and does not grow with its command.
_months: Each place's last Italian month is the file's table by far-side province: Mogadishu and Kismayu 18; Neghelli, Harar and Keren 19; Asmara, Debra Markos, Addis Ababa, Massawa and Dessie 20; Assab and Jimma 22; Gondar 27. Kufra 19. The places the pages do not date stand at the file's derived months with their marks: Belet Uen, Gabredarre (D), Obbia and Bender Cassim (U) at 19, the later month of '18 or 19', since they lie behind Mogadishu (25 February) on the road north; Mekele 21 and Lekemti 23, 'at the latest'. Where two pages disagree inside a month the month stands (Massawa, Dessie, Mega, Agibar, Wolchefit); Jimma 22 by Playfair, the firmer page.
_notLaid: Not laid: (1) Kurmuk's taking as a dated attack ('_gains'). (2) Sebha and Waw el Kebir: the record is silent. The Fezzan's rows have no last month: it stays Italian past 28. (3) Vichy's Djibouti after December 1941 (it ended in month 40, when it went over to Free France): beyond the file's months, and no form of a row passes a garrison's ground with it. It is on the after-release list (the design director's 13:43Z).
_facing: The forces facing Italy as the file lists them. The Sudan: the Sudan Defence Force, 0.3 (4,500 men in twenty-one companies), at its record posts (the historian's section 8.1; the design director's 14:36Z and 18:08Z): at Kassala its two motor machine-gun companies and a mounted company, 0.02 (320 of its men, 500 with the police, L), and the other 0.28 shared evenly (D, until the historian has counts) over the five seats the pages give, El Obeid (the Camel Corps), El Fasher (the Western Arab Corps), Juba (the Equatorial Corps), Atbara (the cavalry at Shendi) and Khartoum (the engineers and depots); the three British battalions, 0.3 (all troops 0.6 less the Defence Force, D), which the 5th Indian Division takes in when it comes in month 13 (worth 1, D: the chart's own unit for a division with no men given, replaced when sourced), lent until 22; Gideon Force 0.1 from 17 to 21, posted at Roseires (D: the Sudan side of the frontier it crossed in January 1941; the file's place, Debra Markos, was Italy's until April), and the Brigade d'Orient 0.1 (U) from 18 to 21 at Port Sudan, where it landed. Both are Britain's rows on this chart: the Free French have no flag of their own after France falls. Kenya: the King's African Rifles 1.5; the 11th African Division (0.55, D) at Garissa from 11 to 27 and the 12th (0.55, D) at Wajir from 11: with the two West African brigades, the file's 3.2 for Kenya's troops other than South Africa's at the end of November 1940 ('_later'). Somaliland: Chater's force 0.1, taken off in month 12 (its 0.3 of early August never stood a whole month); the Aden Striking Force 0.2 from 19, posted at Aden, where it was staged for the landing at Berbera of 16 March 1941 (a row is posted where the record raised or staged it and never on a gain: the design director's 14:18Z). The Belgian Congo's expedition, 0.15 (the middle of 0.1 to 0.2), from 19, posted at Malakal (D: on the Nile, the road it came by from the Congo to Gambela, which the file's own text has it take in March 1941), and gone in 24: the file's last month for it is 23, the month Gazzera surrendered to it at Saio (6 July 1941), and a row is gone in the month written, so it is written 24 to stand through 23. Britain's row, since Belgium has fallen and Lekemti, the file's place, is Italy's. Djibouti: the garrison, 1.0 in June 1940 and 0.5 from July, raised in the place ('levy'), so it goes with Djibouti's keeper when France falls. Chad: Leclerc's troops 0.2 from month 12 at Fort-Lamy, a memory row (U), held to Chad (the design director's 14:18Z: Chad's forces stayed and rallied on 26 August 1940), so the row goes with Chad's keeper. The five garrisons the file has standing on 10 June 1940 (the Defence Force, the British battalions, the King's African Rifles, Chater's force and Djibouti's garrison) are laid in month 9: the file's tables begin at 10, the month Italy came into the war, and on this chart Italy's month comes before Britain's and France's, so a row of month 10 would not stand on the day Italy's war opened (D).
_later: The rows the design director ruled on 13:43Z of 22 November 2026, each marked D where the builder's arithmetic stands in for men the pages do not give. The South Africans are Britain's rows (the design director's 14:36Z): the file has them 'UK (S. Africa)', the old chart's South African division is Britain's row, and a dated attack is one country's fight. 27,000 South Africans in Kenya at the end of November 1940, 1.8, a third to each brigade (D). The 1st South African Brigade, 0.6, a row of its own from 12 to 22 (it sailed on 17 July 1940; it took Dessie in April 1941 and sailed from Massawa on 12 June), posted at Wajir (D: it stood with the 12th African Division, whose place in the file is Wajir). The 1st South African Division, the headquarters with the 2nd and 5th Brigades, 1.2, at Marsabit, the file's place, from 16 (the historian's 8.7: its two brigades were at Marsabit at the end of December 1940; the headquarters had landed at Mombasa on 11 November); from 19 less the 2nd Brigade, 0.6; gone in 21 (the headquarters and the 5th Brigade reached Suez on 3 May 1941, and the old chart's own row brings the division to Alexandria in month 21). The 2nd South African Brigade, 0.6 (D), from 19 to 22: posted at Mombasa, where it took ship for Berbera on 22 and 23 March 1941; it reached Suez on 8 June. The West African brigades, 0.3 each (D: the file's 9,000 West Africans in Kenya at the end of November 1940, shared by the two): the 24th Gold Coast at Wajir with the 12th African Division from 15 (D: the month of that count; the pages give it no first month) to 26, the 23rd Nigerian at Garissa with the 11th from 17 to 23. Both stood inside the two African divisions, which are laid at 0.55 each (the design director's 14:36Z: the file's 3.2 for Kenya's troops other than South Africa's at the end of November 1940, less the King's African Rifles' 1.5 and the two brigades' 0.6, shared by the two), so that the file's 3.2 holds in month 17. The 4th Indian Division's loan, at the stops that keep the book (1 and 2): the desert's own corps on the old chart, taken from it in month 17 (the file's 16 to 17: December 1940 to early January 1941) and posted at Port Sudan (D: the pages give its front, Kassala and then Keren, and no landing place; Kassala was Italy's that month), a lent row to month 20; in 20 the 4th Indian Division stands at Alexandria again, as a row of its own, whatever became of the lent one (the record replaced its losses). At the stops that keep no book the corps is its staff's own and stays in the desert.
_depots: The six command seats carry the map's depot mark (the design director's 13:43Z of 22 November 2026, form (i)): Asmara (Eritrea), Gondar (Amhara), Addis Ababa (Shoa and the headquarters), Jimma (Galla-Sidamo), Harar and Mogadishu (Somalia). Italian East Africa was cut off from Italy from June 1940 and lived on its own stocks until each seat was taken (Amba Alagi in May, Gondar on 27 November 1941). As first laid its ground had no depot and the sea to its ports was shut once its war opened, and all twenty rows starved in the fourth month of the war. A depot feeds its owner's army while he holds it and a road to it (game.ts computeSupply); a few provinces left round one are a pocket and live on the town's stores (siege.ts).
_line: The book's line in East Africa, at the stops that keep the book (the design director's 13:43Z of 22 November 2026, form (ii); line.ts). Italy is the one it gives ground to, and it is drawn on the provinces it names and on no other. Italy's own ground, each province to its last Italian month (a span of kind 'own', and the same month under 'back': Britain's staff comes in that month and not before). The file's table gives nineteen; the chart has seventeen more, laid at months derived from the file's own events, marks kept, for the historian's check: Debra Tabor 23 (F: it surrendered on 6 July 1941 to forces the Patriots led); Asosa 19 (L: the Belgian Congo's force was there about 11 March 1941); Gambela 19 (F: taken on 25 March 1941); Quoram 21 (F: the 1st South African Brigade's column was there on 8 May 1941; Amba Alagi, in or beside its ground, surrendered on 19 May); Shashamanna 21 (F: the 11th African Division, 14 May 1941); Gore 23 (D: Galla-Sidamo, occupied from 6 July 1941, as Lekemti); Yavello 18 (D: Mega, in its ground, surrendered on 18 February 1941); Dolo 18 (L: found empty before the end of February 1941; a Gold Coast column left it for Neghelli on 17 March (the historian's 8.4)); Dagabur 19 (F: the 23rd Nigerian Brigade, 13 March 1941); Asba Tafari 20 (D: on the road from Harar (26 March) to Addis Ababa (6 April 1941)); Adowa 20 (F: reached from Asmara on 2 April 1941); Waldia 21 (F: the 1st South African Brigade, 1 May 1941); Dangila 19 (U: Gojjam, between Gideon Force's crossing in month 17 and Debra Markos in 20); Moyale 18 (F: entered unopposed on 22 February 1941); Bardera 18 (L: found empty by the 24th Gold Coast Brigade's patrols before the end of February 1941); Baidoa 18 (L: occupied by the 24th Gold Coast Brigade's patrols before the end of February 1941); Ginir 20 (U: between Neghelli (19) and Addis Ababa (20)). The gains (kind 'gain'): Kassala 11 to 17, Gallabat 11 to 18, Kurmuk from 11 (its end is not in the pages: 18, as Gallabat's, U), Hargeisa and Berbera 12 to 19, and Burao with them (D: British Somaliland whole). Italy's staff takes them by battles won or does not; when a gain's months are over its corps go back inside the line and the empty ground goes back to Britain. 'shut' is the ring Italy never held: every other province next to its own ground or to a gain (Djibouti among them). '18 or 19' stands at 19: a month is whole. At the stops that do not keep the book there is no line and the staffs decide.
_gains: Italy's gains at the stops that keep the book (the design director's 14:36Z, seam c, and 18:08Z of 22 November 2026). Italy's choice 'eastafrica' is dated month 11 (July 1940), a side choice with no chance of its own, never taken against a player's Britain; its dated attacks are Italy's own rows of the one table ('book': 'ITA:eastafrica'). Each force is a row taken out of its command's worth, so no new men. The Kassala force, 0.4 (6,300 foot and horse of the 8,000 the record has there), out of the Eritrea command's 2.8, staged at Keren (D: the board's province next to Kassala; the record's start was Tessenei), took Kassala on 4 July 1940 from the Defence Force's companies there, 0.02: the two rows are the record's figures, and the fight is the game's own. The Gallabat force, a colonial battalion, 0.05 (D: the file's own 0.1 for the two battalions of Gideon Force), out of the Amhara command's 4.0 and of Gondar's 2.7 from month 21, staged at Gondar, took Gallabat the same day; the pages give no defender there. Nasi's force for British Somaliland, 1.95 (the middle of the pages' 24,000 and 35,000: ranges stand at their middles, the design director's 18:08Z), drawn in month 12 from the Harar command's worth and staged at Harar: Hargeisa on 5 August 1940, Tug Argan and Berbera on 19 August, and Burao with them (D: Italy held all British Somaliland by 19 August). When a gain's months are over its corps go back inside the line. Kurmuk (a colonial battalion against 55 police on 7 July 1940) is not a dated attack: it is the staff's to take in the gain's months.
_attacks: Britain's takings at the stops that keep the book (the design director's 14:17Z and 14:36Z of 22 November 2026: China's form, one map). Britain's choice 'eastafrica' is dated month 17 (January 1941) and is taken on its date with Italy the computer's; it is a side choice with no chance of its own, so at the stops that keep no book it is never taken and the staff decides. Each province Italy holds is a dated attack of that choice's ('book': 'UK:eastafrica'; stations.ts: a dated attack that names its own choice is that country's row), in the province's month on the line, by the rows the record has taking it, from the ground they came by. A row's month on the line is Italy's last there: its garrison row is gone in that month before Britain's turn in it, so most are walked into unfought, and one that finds an enemy in the field is the game's own fight. A row that cannot go in is owed, and is over when its place is Britain's some other way. By the record: Kassala was found empty on 19 January 1941 (the 4th and 5th Indian Divisions); the 1st South African Division took Mega (Yavello) on 18 February; the 12th African Division with the 1st South African and 24th Gold Coast Brigades took Kismayu on 14 February, and the Gold Coast Brigade's patrols went up the Juba before the month was out (Bardera, Baidoa, Dolo), then to Neghelli (22 March) and Ginir; the 11th African Division with the 23rd Nigerian Brigade took Mogadishu (25 February) and, the 1st South African Brigade with it from March, went by Belet Uen, Gabredarre and Dagabur (13 March) to Jijiga and Harar (26 March), Asba Tafari and Addis Ababa (6 April); the 1st South African Brigade went on to Dessie (26 April), Waldia, Quoram and Amba Alagi (Mekele's ground, 19 May) with the 5th Indian Division from Asmara (1 April) and Adowa; the Brigade d'Orient was at Keren (27 March) and Massawa (8 April); Gideon Force went by Dangila to Debra Markos (4 April); the two Punjab battalions from Aden landed at Berbera (16 March) and Assab (11 June); the Belgian Congo's force took Asosa, Gambela and Gazzera's surrender at Saio (Gore, with Lekemti); Jimma fell to the 11th African Division on 21 June and Gondar to the 12th on 27 November. Marks: the months are the line's (F where the file dates the place; the seventeen derived months keep their marks). Who took each place is the historian's (section 8 of the file) where the pages give it; for the rest it is D, the row whose road the place lies on. Not laid: Obbia and Bender Cassim (no force in the pages), and Debra Tabor (it surrendered on 6 July 1941 to forces the Patriots led, who have no row): after its month each is open to Britain's staff, which comes when it comes. Burao, Gallabat and Kurmuk are gains: the line gives them back empty the month after their last. The 2nd South African Brigade is in no row: it is its staff's own.
